title: NEET Paper Leaked Thrice in Five Years, Yet No One Has Been Held Accountable: K. Annamalai
excerpt: The former BJP Tamil Nadu chief's sharp criticism of the Centre comes as a CBI probe reveals insider involvement, student suicides mount, and tens of thousands march on Parliament.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • NEET exam paper leaked thrice in five years, raising accountability concerns.
  • 2026 breach led to the first full cancellation of NEET in its history.
  • Student suicides have surged, with at least twelve deaths linked to the 2026 exam crisis.
  • Protests have erupted nationwide, demanding reforms and accountability from the government.
  • Former BJP leader K. Annamalai criticizes the Centre's handling of the NEET crisis.

K. Annamalai, who resigned as BJP's Tamil Nadu president earlier this year, has broken ranks with his own party to deliver one of the most pointed indictments yet of the Centre's handling of the NEET examination crisis. "The NEET paper has been leaked thrice in five years, and yet there is no accountability," Annamalai said, referring to confirmed breaches in 2021, 2024, and the most recent compromise in May 2026.

The 2026 Breach: From Exam Hall to CBI Custody

The National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test conducted on May 3, 2026, was taken by approximately 2.27 million aspirants. Within days, allegations surfaced that portions of the question paper matched a widely circulated "guess paper." By May 12, the National Testing Agency cancelled the exam entirely — the first full cancellation in NEET's history.

A CBI investigation subsequently led to multiple arrests, including that of Professor P.V. Kulkarni, a chemistry academic with access to NTA's internal question-bank system, and Manisha Waghmare, identified as an intermediary who allegedly facilitated the leak to coaching networks. Investigators found that roughly 140 questions from a pre-exam document matched the actual test paper — a degree of overlap that rules out coincidence.

A re-examination was held on June 21 under significantly tightened security protocols, including GPS-tracked question paper movement and biometric verification at all centres.

> **""This is a pattern of institutional failure," Annamalai said."**

A Pattern of Failures

The 2026 leak is not an isolated incident. A review of NEET's troubled history shows at least five major compromises since the exam was made mandatory for all medical admissions:

  • 2015: Question paper leaked in Haryana; multiple arrests but no systemic reform followed.
  • 2016: Impersonation racket uncovered across multiple states.
  • 2021: Answer key manipulation detected after results were published.
  • 2024: Paper leak traced to a Patna-based coaching syndicate; the controversy contributed to nationwide protests.
  • 2026: The most extensive breach yet, prompting full cancellation and CBI intervention.

"This is a pattern of institutional failure," Annamalai said. "Students prepare for years, families invest their life savings, and the system fails them repeatedly. Where is the structural reform?"

Student Protests Intensify

Impact of the 2026 NEET Crisis
›Approximately 2.27 million aspirants took the exam.
›First full cancellation of NEET in history.
›Roughly 140 questions matched a leaked document.
›Tightened security protocols implemented for re-examination.

Anger over the examination system has moved well beyond social media. On July 20, thousands of students and activists attempted a "Sansad Chalo" (march to Parliament) in New Delhi, which was met with tear gas and water cannons by police. At least twelve students who had appeared for the 2026 NEET examination have died by suicide since the cancellation — a grim statistic that has galvanised the protest movement.

Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the agitation with a hunger strike, calling the crisis "a symptom of deeper institutional rot." Protest solidarity marches have since spread to Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, and other cities, with demonstrators demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and a complete overhaul of the NTA.

Political Fault Lines

Annamalai's criticism is notable precisely because it comes from within the ruling party's ecosystem. Having left the BJP over what he described as disagreements on organisational direction, the former IPS officer has positioned himself as an independent voice — though his comments have drawn sharp reactions from party loyalists who accuse him of opportunism.

Student Protests and Responses
›Thousands marched to Parliament on July 20, met with police force.
›At least twelve student suicides linked to the NEET crisis.
›Protests spread to major cities: Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad.
›Demands include resignation of Union Education Minister.

Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi — both of whom were briefly detained during separate NEET-related protests — have demanded a Supreme Court-monitored investigation. A petition seeking exactly that is currently before the court.

For the millions of NEET aspirants and their families, the political manoeuvring matters less than a straightforward question: when will the system be fixed?
